records.note: Stated intent to start the author's own psychiatric practice in the metaverse ('I am not joking'). The author's own organization decides the outcome; a clinic opening by the forecaster is a commitment, not a forecast.
Release of the author's own show audio to paid subscribers of his own Substack. Own publication; the outcome is under the forecaster's control. It is also outside the five areas.
Release of the author's own edited podcast to the public in fall 2021. Own publication; the outcome is under the forecaster's control. It is also outside the five areas.

Media coverage of suicides 'will continue to improve' is a claim about journalism, not a regulatory, trial, company, payer or practice outcome. The 'hope' framing and the comparative 'improve' with no benchmark or series would also make it VAGUE.
The author's own weekly Clubhouse AMA schedule. Own event under the forecaster's control; the sentence is also descriptive and asserts no future state beyond his own plan.

event.asset: ERISA enforcement over abortion-related health coverage after Dobbs
event.entity: US Department of Labor (EBSA) or US Department of Justice
event.title: Federal ERISA enforcement action over post-Dobbs abortion coverage
event.proposition: A federal agency (the Department of Labor or the Department of Justice) brings an ERISA-based enforcement action concerning abortion-related health coverage or care after the Dobbs decision.
event.criterion: TRUE on the docket date of a filed federal complaint, or the date of a Department of Labor or Department of Justice press release, that initiates or announces an ERISA-based federal enforcement action (a civil suit, an administrative enforcement order or a filed settlement) whose stated legal basis is ERISA and whose subject is abortion-related health coverage or care after the Dobbs decision. Guidance documents, FAQs, public statements, amicus briefs and private lawsuits are not federal enforcement actions.

resolution_source.name: DOL/EBSA and DOJ press releases; federal court dockets (CourtListener)

readings: 'ERISA is next' is read as the next federal enforcement action after the EMTALA suit the author describes, brought under ERISA. The author does not name the enforcing agency, so an action by either the Department of Labor or the Department of Justice counts.
court_outcome is the closest template for a federal enforcement action. The event resolves on the initiation or announcement of the action, not on a later verdict.

records.phrase: ERISA is next. ... Enforcement is coming.
records.stage_note: Per the author's own words on 2 July 2022: the DOJ sued Ohio over EMTALA that day and the Department of Labor had 'weighed in' on ERISA fiduciary duties in Massachusetts the week before; no ERISA enforcement action yet. No base-rate class covers federal enforcement actions.
records.note: Sequence forecast: EMTALA suit first, ERISA action next. Bin A on 'is coming' (lexicon A phrase in the claim). The horizon words 'next' and 'is coming' are not deadlines, so the item is undated (24-month window from 2022-07-02). Not a report: no source is cited and no date is named. Not affiliated.

The text 'Enforcement is coming. This is not a drill.' is the second half of the owen-0048 quote from the same 2 July 2022 update. The first row (owen-0048) stands and carries the ERISA enforcement event. On its own, 'Enforcement' names no action and would be VAGUE.

Three-part consequence claim. 'Physician shortages' and 'dead patients' are quantifiers with no countable set, threshold or series; 'tax liability for large employers' names no deciding body or mechanism; 'catastrophic' is a slogan. The tax claim appears as a present-tense legal conclusion in owen-0056.

Fictional analogy (a chest-stabbing law). The underlying claim, that families sue doctors in ban states and win and that malpractice carriers have 'a problem', names no case, countable set, threshold or deciding body.
Mechanism claim. 'Uninsured doctors won't practice in states with bans' has no countable set, series or threshold, and no deciding body.

'Doctors will flee those states' names no metric, threshold or series, and 'doctors' has no countable set. The condition ('as soon as patients sue') is also undefined. A quantity event would require inventing both a series and a threshold.
Mechanism claim about non-comprehensive health plans plus a present-tense legal interpretation ('no one can legally sell these'). No entity, observable event, benchmark or threshold.
'No med school education in such states' over an unbounded time ('over time') has no countable set, series, threshold or deadline.
Present-tense legal interpretation ('Now, every employer ... owes the IRS'). The words state a legal conclusion as information; no future action by the IRS, a court or any other body is asserted.

Compound restatement of the post's consequence chain (uninsurable doctors, patients without care, a 'massive tax bill' for employers). No threshold, series or deciding body; 'massive' and 'the wreckage that follows' are not benchmarks or deadlines.
'A hell of a lot of lawsuits' is a quantifier with no countable set; 'catastrophic for most patients, their employers, doctors and insurance conglomerates' has no benchmark or series.
Slogan ('Buckle up. It's going to get bumpy.'). No entity, event, benchmark or threshold.

A colleague's interview question about the Ryan-Haight Act, reported by the author. The author calls the question important but asserts no future state; reinstatement of the in-person rule is not predicted in his words.
Capability denial ('not a problem Cerebral can solve') with no observable event, benchmark or series for the specialist shortage.
Whether former Cerebral clinicians 'have their practice tracked thereafter' has no observable event, series, countable set or deciding body.
'Many will not continue to take insurance' is a quantifier with no countable set or series; 'probably charging more now' is a present hedge with no benchmark.

'May be guilty of a variety of regulatory and other missteps or crimes' names no deciding body and no specific charge or determination; 'missteps' is not an observable finding. 'Soon enough' is not a deadline. Writing a court_outcome event would require inventing the set of authorities and the type of determination.

'Have the potential to relieve suffering vastly more than current treatments' is a possibility statement with a comparative and no benchmark, metric or series. The testable SNT forecast in this post is owen-0070.
Definitional claim: if the SNT results are replicated, they meet the dictionary definition of 'cure'. The conditional is the premise; the author asserts nothing about whether replication occurs.

Present-tense description of the treatment's properties (five days, remission for more than 50 percent, no medication, minimal risk, durable effect), taken from existing study results. No future trial or event is asserted; the ironic framing does not change the descriptive content.

Description of SNT's regulatory status at the statement date (not FDA cleared, Breakthrough designation, process 'sped up'). No clearance decision, probability word or date is asserted; 'not yet' is read as words, not as a call.

'When it is broadly offered' is a presupposition with no threshold or series; the asserted clause ('we will understand enough about the risks and benefits') is a knowledge claim with no observable event.

event.asset: SNT (Stanford Neuromodulation Therapy, accelerated iTBS) for depression
event.entity: Magnus Medical (SNT commercial sponsor) and Stanford University (SNT developer); other sponsors of accelerated iTBS trials
event.title: SNT or accelerated iTBS: subsequent RCT positive on the primary depression endpoint
event.proposition: A randomized controlled trial of SNT or another accelerated iTBS protocol for depression, reported after 11 July 2022, meets its prespecified primary endpoint with statistical significance.
event.criterion: TRUE on the date of the first sponsor topline release, ClinicalTrials.gov results posting or peer-reviewed publication dated after 2022-07-11 that reports a randomized controlled trial of SNT (Stanford Neuromodulation Therapy, the accelerated intermittent theta-burst TMS protocol commercialized by Magnus Medical) or another accelerated iTBS protocol for a depressive disorder, distinct from the Stanford SNT trial already published at the statement date, in which the prespecified primary efficacy endpoint met statistical significance versus the control arm as reported by the sponsor or the authors. Open-label series, secondary endpoints and pooled analyses do not count.

resolution_source.name: ClinicalTrials.gov results and peer-reviewed publication (PubMed); sponsor topline release

readings: 'SNT and similar approaches' is read as SNT or another accelerated iTBS protocol (several iTBS sessions a day over about five days), per the author's own description of SNT in the post.

'demonstrate statistical significance' is read as the primary efficacy endpoint meeting significance in a randomized controlled trial; the author names randomized controlled trials as the test in the same post (owen-0072).
'and be Helpful' is split off as owen-0070-b and is not written into this event.

records.phrase: I believe that SNT and similar approaches will demonstrate
records.stage_note: SNT at the statement date, per the author: one published Stanford randomized trial, FDA Breakthrough designation, not FDA cleared. The base-rate table has no trial-result class, so no base rate.
records.note: Core SNT forecast, first half of an 'A and B' claim. Bin A on 'will', the strongest phrase in the claim sentence ('I believe' alone would be B); owen-0071 states near-certainty for the same forecast. No deadline words; no trial is named, so the ClinicalTrials.gov table rule cannot apply; undated panel (24 months from 2022-07-11). Not affiliated: Magnus Medical and Stanford are not in the author's affiliation list, though he discloses treating patients with a close analog of SNT (owen-0072).
Second half of the 'A and B' claim in owen-0070: SNT and similar approaches will 'be Helpful'. 'Helpful' has no benchmark, metric or series. The first half is coded at owen-0070-a.

Confidence clause for the owen-0070 forecast ('amazing' as the outcome of subsequent research, near-certain). Same forecast in the same post; owen-0070-a stands and already carries bin A. On its own, 'amazing' has no benchmark.

Hedge clause on the same owen-0070 forecast (the randomized controlled trials 'possibly won't' show the expected results). Same event in the same post; owen-0070-a stands. A separate record would score one forecast twice. The sentence also discloses that the author treats patients with a close analog of SNT.
Claim about the field's communication behavior and that it 'will be a poor choice'. No entity, observable event, benchmark or series.
'I hope ... that standard is going to be about five days' names no series, threshold or defining body for 'standard'; 'in the very near future' is not a deadline. The first sentence is normative.
Present-tense assessment of the 988 launch ('It doesn't, at least not right now'). 'Move the needle' is a slogan; no future state is asserted.
'Any of our patients will be meaningfully impacted in the near term' has no benchmark, countable set or series; 'in the near term' is not a deadline.

Doubt that 988 funding 'will be sustained or enough to meet increased demand' names no threshold, period or series. A funding event would require inventing a level and a fiscal year from the figures the author cites.
Hedged mechanism claim ('the caller may ... dial 988') about misrouted overdose calls. No countable set, series, threshold or deciding body.

Verbatim quote from Snook (Treatment Advocacy Center), cited by the authors as evidence. Not the forecaster's own words. Even if adopted, 'these tragic outcomes will continue' has no series or threshold, and the condition ('until we reform the public policies') is undefined.
Conditional ('can save lives if more effort and funding is directed'). Neither the condition nor 'save lives' has a threshold, series or observable event.
A visionary 'Elon Musk for Healthcare' will arrive. No entity, observable event, benchmark or deadline.

States a put-option position on LifeStance and asks a rhetorical question. No future state is asserted in words and no confidence phrase is given, so no bin can be set. A share-price event inferred from the position would also lack a threshold and a date.
